 Week 3–5: Azure architecture, storage, and networking basics
 Week 6–8: Azure security, compliance, and governance
 Week 9–10: Exam preparation and certification attempt
Credentials Earned:
 Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900)
 IBM Cloud Essentials Badge

Data Analytics — 12–16 weeks
Data skills are the most broadly applicable technical competency in the modern economy. Entry-level data
analyst roles pay $45,000–$65,000 and exist across every industry sector.
Weekly Structure:
 Week 1–3: Spreadsheet fundamentals and data organization (Google / GCFGlobal)
 Week 4–7: SQL basics and database querying (Google Data Analytics Certificate)
 Week 8–11: Data visualization with Tableau and Google Sheets
 Week 12–14: Capstone project and portfolio development
 Week 15–16: Job application support and employer introductions
Credentials Earned:
 Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
 IBM Data Analyst Badge
AI Tools and Workflow Automation — 4–6 weeks
The most immediately practical pathway for workers displaced by AI specifically. Teaches participants to
work with AI tools rather than be replaced by them. Applicable across every industry and role type.
Weekly Structure:
 Week 1–2: AI fundamentals and how large language models work (IBM SkillsBuild)
 Week 3–4: Prompt engineering for workplace tasks (Anthropic / IBM)
 Week 5–6: Workflow automation tools and AI-assisted productivity
Credentials Earned:
 IBM AI Fundamentals Badge
 Anthropic AI Fluency Certificate
Microsoft Office and Administrative Technology — 4–8 weeks
The foundational pathway for participants moving into administrative, clerical, and office support roles. Broad
applicability across every employment sector.
Weekly Structure:

 Week 1–2: Word processing and document creation (GCFGlobal / MS Learn)
 Week 3–4: Spreadsheets and data organization (GCFGlobal / MS Learn)
 Week 5–6: Presentations and professional communication tools
 Week 7–8: Email, calendar management, and Microsoft 365 ecosystem
Credentials Earned:
 Microsoft Office Specialist Certification (exam-based)
 GCFGlobal Completion Certificate
NON-TECHNOLOGY PATHWAYS — DETAIL
Not every displaced worker is positioned for a technology career. The mandate applies equally to the factory
worker, the retail manager, the truck driver, and the office clerk. These pathways equip participants for
stable, dignified employment across a broad range of industries and skill levels.
Digital Literacy Foundations — 2–4 weeks · GCFGlobal / Khan Academy
For participants with minimal technology experience. Covers computer basics, internet navigation, email, and
smartphone proficiency. The prerequisite for every other pathway. No participant is turned away for lack of
baseline skills.
Topics Covered:
 Basic computer operation and file management
 Internet safety and email communication
 Smartphone and tablet proficiency
 Introduction to productivity tools
Financial Literacy and Personal Finance — 4–6 weeks · Khan Academy
Foundational financial knowledge that multiplies the value of every other pathway. Budgeting, banking,
credit, taxes, and benefits navigation. Especially critical for participants emerging from long-term
displacement.
Topics Covered:
 Budgeting and expense tracking
 Banking, savings, and credit fundamentals
 Tax basics and benefit programs

 Financial goal setting and planning
Small Business and Self-Employment Basics — 6–8 weeks · Khan Academy / Coursera
For participants whose best path to stability is self-employment. Covers business structure, basic
accounting, marketing, and customer acquisition. Pairs with the Institute's network of mentors and micro-loan
referrals.
Topics Covered:
 Business structure and legal basics
 Basic bookkeeping and record-keeping
 Marketing and customer acquisition fundamentals
 Pricing, invoicing, and cash flow management
Customer Service and Retail Skills — 3–4 weeks · Coursera / IBM SkillsBuild
High-demand skills across retail, hospitality, healthcare, and service industries. IBM's customer service
training leads to a recognized badge. Pairs with Institute employer network for direct placement.
Topics Covered:
 Communication and de-escalation skills
 Point of sale and transaction processing
 Customer relationship management basics
 Professional workplace conduct
Administrative and Office Professional — 6–8 weeks · MS Learn / GCFGlobal / LinkedIn Learning
Prepares participants for receptionist, administrative assistant, data entry, and office coordinator roles. One
of the broadest employment pipelines available to adult learners regardless of prior experience.
Topics Covered:
 Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook proficiency
 Business writing and professional communication
 Calendar and scheduling management
 Basic bookkeeping and records management

Workplace Readiness and Professional Skills — 2–4 weeks · IBM SkillsBuild
The foundational cohort orientation for all participants regardless of pathway. Covers professional conduct,
workplace communication, time management, and navigating workplace culture. IBM issues a recognized
digital badge upon completion.
Topics Covered:
 Professional communication and workplace norms
 Time management and task prioritization
 Conflict resolution and teamwork
 Job search strategy and interview preparation
English Language and Communication Skills — Ongoing · Khan Academy / GCFGlobal
Available as a standalone pathway or concurrent support for any other program. Reading, writing, and
professional communication for participants whose first language is not English or who need foundational
literacy support.
Topics Covered:
 Reading comprehension and vocabulary
 Business writing and professional email
 Verbal communication and presentation basics
 Grammar and mechanics for workplace documents
COHORT DELIVERY MODEL
All pathways are delivered in cohorts of 8–15 participants. The cohort model is not a logistical preference —
it is a theological conviction. Human beings were not created to learn alone, and community accountability is
one of the most powerful drivers of completion in adult workforce training.
Week 0 — Intake and Assessment
All participants complete intake, aptitude assessment, and pathway selection. Digital literacy baseline is
assessed. Participants without device access are connected to loaner devices through library and
community partnerships.

Week 1 — Cohort Orientation
All participants complete the IBM Workplace Readiness pathway together regardless of their individual track.
This builds cohort identity, establishes shared expectations, and provides an IBM digital credential
immediately.
Weeks 2–12 — Primary Pathway Training
Participants work through their individual pathway using the free platform infrastructure. Weekly cohort
check-ins provide accountability and peer support. Institute staff provide navigation support and
troubleshooting.
Final 2 Weeks — Portfolio and Placement
Resume building, LinkedIn profile creation, mock interviews, and direct connections to the Institute's
employer network. Certification exam support where applicable. Graduation and credential presentation.
Post-Graduation — Alumni Network
Graduates enter the Institute's alumni network and are encouraged to mentor incoming cohorts. This fulfills
the theological obligation of the equipped to equip others, and builds the organizational community over time.
PARTNERSHIP AND DONATION PIPELINE
The Institute actively pursues formal partnerships with the following organizations for curriculum donation,
access, and co-delivery:
IBM SkillsBuild
Nonprofit organization partnership — apply at skillsbuild.org/organizations-supporting-adult-learners.
Provides cohort-guided learning experiences, IBM credentials, and job fair access.
Google Career Certificates Fund
Nonprofit partnership through Merit America and Year Up frameworks. Contact grow.google/certificates for
nonprofit access programs.
Microsoft for Nonprofits
Free Microsoft 365 and Azure credits for qualifying nonprofits. The Institute qualifies upon receiving EIN.
Apply at microsoft.com/nonprofits.
Coursera for Social Impact
Free Coursera access for qualifying workforce development nonprofits. Apply at coursera.org/social-impact.

Goodwill Industries of Central Texas
Local Goodwill chapter operates its own workforce training programs and may partner for facility use,
referrals, and co-delivery.
Austin Public Library
Free LinkedIn Learning access for all cardholders. Computer access and device lending programs available
for participants without devices.
Austin Community College Continuing Education
ACC offers free and low-cost workforce training and may partner for facility use and credential alignment.
Per Scholas
National nonprofit delivering free tech training — potential referral and co-delivery partner rather than
competitor, as our populations overlap.
Workforce Solutions Capital Area
Austin-area workforce development board administering WIOA funds. Primary target for government contract
funding of program delivery.
